title: MemTrapBench: Benchmarking Cognitive Traps in LLM Memory Use

analysis.tldr: MemTrapBench constructs 1,050 cases where related prior history can fixate reasoning or distort beliefs. Every tested memory/context package trails no-memory on the aggregate stress-test score, but the benchmark deliberately makes the current query independently solvable and plants a trap; it measures conditional susceptibility, not memory's net real-world utility.
analysis.problem: Even accurate and relevant retrieved memories can be inapplicable or cognitively anchoring for the current task. Existing benchmarks emphasize extraction and recall rather than the downstream harm of using memory.
analysis.core_idea: Generate long histories containing Task Boundary, Cognitive Bias, Trauma, or Safety traps, compare the same model with and without memory, and add limited trap-free controls. AdaptiveMem is a query-time system prompt that asks the consumer to check current applicability before using retrieved history.

memory_design.write: The benchmark supplies generated interaction histories to FullText or four memory frameworks; it does not isolate their write mechanisms.
memory_design.organize: LightMem, MemOS, SimpleMem, and EverMemOS use different compression and organization packages whose configurations and budgets are not matched.
memory_design.read: Retrieved or full-history memory is supplied before the same final query. AdaptiveMem adds a taxonomy-matched applicability check at answer time.
memory_design.update_forget: No evolving update, expiry, conflict repair, or forgetting policy is evaluated; the measured boundary is admission after retrieval.

compared_to: The same answer model with no history, on final queries deliberately designed to be independently solvable
Trap-inducing versus limited trap-free history controls for Task Boundary and Trauma
The same FullText, LightMem, or EverMemOS framework with versus without the AdaptiveMem system prompt
analysis.evidence: On Gemini, no-memory averages 85.16 while the strongest memory arm, EverMemOS, reaches 71.17; on Qwen, no-memory is 81.83 and the strongest memory/context arm is FullText at 70.99, with LightMem at 70.13. In limited matched controls, Task Boundary scores 92.29 no-memory, 94.39 trap-free, and 31.05 with the trap; Trauma is 86.73, 84.33, and 69.43. AdaptiveMem adds 11.8/14.9/11.3 points on Gemini and 4.2/2.5/2.6 on Qwen across three memory arms, without uncertainty estimates.
analysis.why_it_matters: Successful retrieval is not sufficient: an actor needs a read-time applicability or admission decision that preserves useful memory while rejecting misleading prior context. Harm should be measured at the consumer behavior, not inferred from stored content alone.
limitations: This is an adversarial synthetic stress test in which every final query is solvable without history and prior dialogue is generated to plant a trap; it does not estimate trap prevalence or memory's net utility.
Trap-free controls cover only Task Boundary and Trauma, with incomplete subset, model, and framework reporting.
Headline percentages average four LLM-judged dimensions; Table 1 has no confidence intervals, paired tests, or repeated-run variance, and judge absolute scores differ materially.
Framework versions, configurations, retrieval budgets, and full ingestion/access/maintenance costs are unreported; the linked repository was an empty placeholder when verified.
AdaptiveMem explicitly names the benchmark's four trap types and uses random 200-item slices without uncertainty or a length-matched neutral prompt, so it supports benchmark-aligned mitigation only.
